```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/01_sample_sheet.R")

phen_cols <- c(Normal = "#1f78b4", Lesion = "#ff7f00", Tumor = "#e31a1c")

PROJECT_ROOT <- normalizePath("..")
CSV_PATH     <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT,
                  "IJGA_Oral Leukoplakia_x8_4-28-26",
                  "IJGA_Oral Leukoplakia_x8_4-28-26.csv")
IDAT_DIR     <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT,
                  "IJGA_Oral Leukoplakia_x8_IDATs_4-28-26")

```

# Cohort

```{r cohort}
ss <- build_sample_sheet(CSV_PATH, IDAT_DIR)
ss
```

`r nrow(ss)` samples on a single EPIC v2 chip. The design is patient-paired:
formal differential analysis is the **paired Normal vs Lesion** test (n = 3
pairs); the single tumor sample is shown descriptively against that background.

# 1. Read & normalize with sesame

```{r normalize, cache = TRUE}
sesameDataCacheAll()        # one-time; idempotent

prefixes <- setNames(ss$Basename, ss$Sample_Name)

## SigDF list — keep for QC and SNP/sex inference
sdfs <- openSesame(prefixes, platform = "EPICv2", func = NULL,
                   BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam())

## Normalized betas (CpG x sample), with pOOBAH masking + noob + dye-bias
betas <- openSesame(sdfs, func = getBetas)
colnames(betas) <- ss$Sample_Name
dim(betas)
```

# 2. QC

```{r qc-stats}
## inferSex() takes betas (sesame >= 1.2x); passing the SigDF errored and
## silently returned NA for every sample in the first version of this report.
safe_sex <- function(s) {
  tryCatch(as.character(inferSex(getBetas(s), platform = "EPICv2")),
           error = function(e) NA_character_)
}
qc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sdfs), function(i) {
  s <- sdfs[[i]]
  data.frame(
    Sample              = ss$Sample_Name[i],
    Group               = as.character(ss$Group[i]),
    Patient             = ss$Patient[i],
    Unmasked_fraction   = round(mean(!is.na(getBetas(s))), 4),   # pOOBAH + design/quality masks
    pOOBAH_pass_rate    = round(mean(pOOBAH(s, return.pval = TRUE) < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    Mean_intensity      = round(meanIntensity(s), 1),
    Inferred_sex        = safe_sex(s),
    stringsAsFactors    = FALSE
  )
}))
qc
write.csv(qc, file.path(TBL_DIR, "qc_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r qc-density, fig.cap="Beta density per sample (post-normalization)"}
df_dens <- as.data.frame(betas) |>
  rownames_to_column("CpG") |>
  pivot_longer(-CpG, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Beta") |>
  filter(!is.na(Beta)) |>
  left_join(ss[, c("Sample_Name","Group","Patient")], by = c("Sample" = "Sample_Name"))

ggplot(df_dens, aes(Beta, colour = Sample, linetype = Group)) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 0.4, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  labs(x = expression(beta), y = "density")
```

# 3. Probe filtering

```{r filter, cache = TRUE}
## (a) drop probes masked in > 25% of samples
frac_na <- rowMeans(is.na(betas))
betas_keep <- betas[frac_na <= 0.25, , drop = FALSE]

## (b) drop chrX/chrY (sex annotated as Unknown for all samples)
manifest <- sesameData_getManifestGRanges("EPICv2")
auto     <- names(manifest)[as.character(seqnames(manifest)) %in% paste0("chr", 1:22)]
betas_keep <- betas_keep[rownames(betas_keep) %in% auto, , drop = FALSE]

## Two parallel matrices:
##   betas_u  — uncollapsed (EPIC v2 IlmnID with _BC11/_TC21 suffix). Needed by DMRcate.
##   betas_f  — collapsed to one β per CpG. Used for DMPs / PCA / heatmaps / trajectories.
betas_u <- betas_keep[complete.cases(betas_keep), , drop = FALSE]
betas_f <- betasCollapseToPfx(betas_keep)
betas_f <- betas_f[complete.cases(betas_f), , drop = FALSE]

cat(sprintf("Probes after filtering — uncollapsed: %d, collapsed: %d (of %d original)\n",
            nrow(betas_u), nrow(betas_f), nrow(betas)))

mvals   <- beta_to_m(betas_f)
mvals_u <- beta_to_m(betas_u)
```

# 4. Exploratory — all 8 samples

```{r pca, fig.cap="PCA of top-5000 most variable CpGs (β-values)"}
n_top <- 5000
v <- matrixStats::rowVars(betas_f)
top <- order(v, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(n_top, length(v)))]
pca <- prcomp(t(betas_f[top, ]), scale. = FALSE)

pct <- round(100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2), 1)
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:3]) |>
  rownames_to_column("Sample") |>
  left_join(ss, by = c("Sample" = "Sample_Name"))

ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = Group, shape = Patient, label = Sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 20, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Normal = "#1f78b4",
                                 Lesion = "#ff7f00",
                                 Tumor  = "#e31a1c")) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%s%%)", pct[1]),
       y = sprintf("PC2 (%s%%)", pct[2])) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

```{r corr-heatmap, fig.cap="Sample-sample Pearson correlation on top-variable CpGs"}
cor_mat <- cor(betas_f[top, ], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
ann <- data.frame(Group = ss$Group, Patient = ss$Patient,
                  row.names = ss$Sample_Name)
pheatmap(cor_mat, annotation_col = ann, annotation_row = ann,
         display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.3f", fontsize = 8)
```

## 4b. What drives PC1? Tissue composition

Bulk oral biopsies differ greatly in epithelial, stromal and immune content.
EpiDISH (RPC, epithelial/fibroblast/immune reference; the same method used for
GSE204943) estimates these fractions from the methylation data itself.

```{r pca-composition, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.2}
data(centEpiFibIC.m)
cell_frac <- epidish(beta.m = betas_f, ref.m = centEpiFibIC.m, method = "RPC")$estF
comp_df <- data.frame(Sample = rownames(cell_frac), round(cell_frac, 3),
                      PC1 = round(pca$x[rownames(cell_frac), 1], 1)) |>
  left_join(ss[, c("Sample_Name", "Group", "Patient")], by = c("Sample" = "Sample_Name"))
comp_df
write.csv(comp_df, file.path(TBL_DIR, "cell_composition_epidish.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
r_pc1_epi <- cor(comp_df$PC1, comp_df$Epi)

ggplot(comp_df, aes(Epi, PC1, colour = Group, shape = Patient)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Sample), size = 2.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = phen_cols) +
  labs(x = "Epithelial fraction (EpiDISH)", y = "PC1 of the all-sample PCA",
       title = sprintf("PC1 vs epithelial fraction: r = %.2f", r_pc1_epi)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

**PC1 is mostly a tissue-composition axis** (r = `r round(r_pc1_epi, 2)` with
epithelial fraction). Samples that sit "near the tumour" on PC1 are the
immune/stroma-rich ones (the PVL lesion is the most immune-rich sample, in line
with its lymphoid-dominant Xenium composition). PC1 position therefore cannot be
read as malignant potential; section 11 gives a composition-adjusted continuum.

# 5. Differential methylation — paired Normal vs Lesion

```{r dmp, cache = TRUE}
paired_patients <- c("Patient 3", "Patient 4", "Patient 5")
keep <- ss$Patient %in% paired_patients & ss$Group %in% c("Normal", "Lesion")
ss_p <- droplevels(ss[keep, ])
M_p  <- mvals[, ss_p$Sample_Name]

Group   <- factor(as.character(ss_p$Group), levels = c("Normal", "Lesion"))
Patient <- factor(ss_p$Patient)

design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + Group + Patient)
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))
contrasts <- makeContrasts(LesionVsNormal = GroupLesion - GroupNormal,
                           levels = design)

fit  <- lmFit(M_p, design)
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, robust = TRUE, trend = TRUE)

dmp <- topTable(fit2, coef = "LesionVsNormal",
                number = Inf, sort.by = "P", adjust.method = "BH")

## annotate with delta-beta and nearest gene
B_p <- betas_f[, ss_p$Sample_Name]
mean_lesion <- rowMeans(B_p[, ss_p$Group == "Lesion"], na.rm = TRUE)
mean_normal <- rowMeans(B_p[, ss_p$Group == "Normal"], na.rm = TRUE)
dmp$delta_beta <- mean_lesion[rownames(dmp)] - mean_normal[rownames(dmp)]

## EPIC v2 anno's Name carries a replicate suffix (e.g. cg25324105_BC11);
## our DMP rownames are the collapsed CpG IDs (no suffix). Strip and dedupe.
anno_v2 <- minfi::getAnnotation(IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICv2anno.20a1.hg38)
anno_v2$cpg <- sub("_[^_]+$", "", anno_v2$Name)
anno_v2 <- anno_v2[!duplicated(anno_v2$cpg), , drop = FALSE]
m <- match(rownames(dmp), anno_v2$cpg)
dmp$chr  <- anno_v2$chr[m]
dmp$pos  <- anno_v2$pos[m]
dmp$gene <- anno_v2$UCSC_RefGene_Name[m]
dmp$gene <- vapply(strsplit(dmp$gene, ";"), function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(unique(x), collapse = ";")
}, character(1))
dmp$relation_to_island <- anno_v2$Relation_to_Island[m]

write.csv(dmp, file.path(TBL_DIR, "dmp_lesion_vs_normal.csv"))
head(dmp[, c("logFC","delta_beta","P.Value","adj.P.Val","chr","pos","gene","relation_to_island")], 25)
```

```{r volcano, fig.cap="Volcano: paired Lesion vs Normal"}
vd <- dmp |>
  mutate(sig = case_when(
    adj.P.Val < 0.05 & delta_beta >  0.1 ~ "hyper",
    adj.P.Val < 0.05 & delta_beta < -0.1 ~ "hypo",
    TRUE                                  ~ "ns"
  ))

ggplot(vd, aes(delta_beta, -log10(P.Value), colour = sig)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(hyper = "#e31a1c", hypo = "#1f78b4", ns = "grey70")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.1, 0.1), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05),  linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = expression(Delta*beta~"(Lesion - Normal)"),
       y = expression(-log[10]~P), colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

# 6. DMRs — DMRcate (paired Normal vs Lesion)

> **Read these as exploratory candidate regions, not significant DMRs.** With
> n = 3 pairs no single CpG passes FDR (minimum adjusted P is shown in the
> table above), and `cpg.annotate()` is run at a permissive FDR of 0.5 so that
> DMRcate has CpGs to build regions from. The resulting smoothed "FDR" values
> do not carry their nominal meaning. Section 6b checks the top candidates
> against the independent GSE204943 cohort.

```{r dmrs, cache = TRUE}
## DMRcate needs uncollapsed EPIC v2 IlmnIDs (with _BC11/_TC21 suffix).
M_u_p <- mvals_u[, ss_p$Sample_Name]

## Use a permissive cpg.annotate FDR (n=3 pairs has limited single-CpG power);
## DMRcate's regional smoothing recovers signal that single-CpG FDR misses.
myanno <- cpg.annotate(
  object       = M_u_p,
  datatype     = "array",
  what         = "M",
  arraytype    = "EPICv2",
  analysis.type = "differential",
  design       = design,
  contrasts    = TRUE,
  cont.matrix  = contrasts,
  coef         = "LesionVsNormal",
  fdr          = 0.5
)

## Try strict default first; fall back to a raw p-value cutoff if nothing passes.
run_dmrcate <- function() {
  out <- tryCatch(dmrcate(myanno, lambda = 1000, C = 2),
                  error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(out, "error")) {
    msg <- conditionMessage(out)
    if (grepl("no significant CpGs|no DMRs", msg)) {
      message("No DMRs at default cutoff; retrying with pcutoff = 1e-3.")
      out <- tryCatch(dmrcate(myanno, lambda = 1000, C = 2, pcutoff = 1e-3),
                      error = function(e) e)
    }
  }
  if (inherits(out, "error")) {
    message("dmrcate failed: ", conditionMessage(out)); return(NULL)
  }
  out
}

dmrs <- run_dmrcate()

if (!is.null(dmrs)) {
  dmr_ranges <- extractRanges(dmrs, genome = "hg38")
  dmr_df <- as.data.frame(dmr_ranges)
  write.csv(dmr_df, file.path(TBL_DIR, "dmrs_lesion_vs_normal.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("DMRs found: %d\n", length(dmr_ranges)))
  head(dmr_df, 25)
}
```

```{r dmr-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, eval=exists("dmr_ranges") && length(dmr_ranges) > 0}
## Top-3 candidate regions (by Fisher P) across ALL 8 samples, so the tumour
## overlays. Drawn offline: DMRcate::DMR.plot needs an Ensembl connection
## (and, in v1 of this report, was also given collapsed CpG IDs and errored).
top3 <- dmr_ranges[order(dmr_ranges$Fisher)][1:min(3, length(dmr_ranges))]
reg_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(top3), function(i) {
  r <- top3[i]
  sel <- anno_v2$chr == as.character(GenomicRanges::seqnames(r)) &
    anno_v2$pos >= GenomicRanges::start(r) - 2000 & anno_v2$pos <= GenomicRanges::end(r) + 2000
  cps <- intersect(anno_v2$cpg[sel], rownames(betas_f))
  if (length(cps) == 0) return(NULL)
  d <- as.data.frame(betas_f[cps, , drop = FALSE])
  d$pos <- anno_v2$pos[match(cps, anno_v2$cpg)]
  d <- pivot_longer(d, -pos, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Beta")
  d$region <- sprintf("%s:%d-%d  %s", GenomicRanges::seqnames(r), GenomicRanges::start(r),
                      GenomicRanges::end(r), substr(r$overlapping.genes, 1, 30))
  d
}))
reg_df <- left_join(reg_df, ss[, c("Sample_Name", "Group", "Patient")], by = c("Sample" = "Sample_Name"))
ggplot(reg_df, aes(pos / 1e3, Beta, colour = Group, group = Sample)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~region, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = phen_cols) + ylim(0, 1) +
  labs(x = "Position (kb, hg38)", y = expression(beta)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

## 6b. Do the top candidate regions replicate externally?

For each of the 30 strongest candidate regions (by Fisher P): the mean
lesion-minus-own-adjacent Δβ in each pilot patient, and the external Δβ
(OPL − normal, tumour − normal) in GSE204943 over the same CpGs.

```{r dmr-replication, eval = exists("dmr_ranges") && length(dmr_ranges) > 0 && file.exists(file.path(EXT_DIR, "gse_signature.rds"))}
sig_ext <- readRDS(file.path(EXT_DIR, "gse_signature.rds"))
top_dmr <- dmr_ranges[order(dmr_ranges$Fisher)][1:min(30, length(dmr_ranges))]
anno_gr2 <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(anno_v2$chr, IRanges::IRanges(anno_v2$pos, width = 1), cpg = anno_v2$cpg)
pairs_d <- sapply(c("Patient 2", "Patient 3", "Patient 4", "Patient 5"), function(pt) {
  les <- ss$Sample_Name[ss$Patient == pt & ss$Group != "Normal"]
  adj <- ss$Sample_Name[ss$Patient == pt & ss$Group == "Normal"]
  betas_f[, les] - betas_f[, adj]
})
dmr_rep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(top_dmr), function(i) {
  cps <- intersect(anno_gr2$cpg[S4Vectors::subjectHits(GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(top_dmr[i], anno_gr2))],
                   rownames(betas_f))
  e <- sig_ext[sig_ext$cpg %in% cps, ]
  data.frame(region = sprintf("%s:%d-%d", GenomicRanges::seqnames(top_dmr[i]),
                              GenomicRanges::start(top_dmr[i]), GenomicRanges::end(top_dmr[i])),
             genes = substr(top_dmr$overlapping.genes[i], 1, 40), n_cpg = length(cps),
             t(round(colMeans(pairs_d[cps, , drop = FALSE]), 3)),
             GSE_OPL_minus_N = round(mean(e$d_OvN), 3), GSE_T_minus_N = round(mean(e$d_TvN), 3),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
names(dmr_rep)[4:7] <- c("d_P2_tumor", "d_P3", "d_P4", "d_P5")
dmr_rep$replicates_GSE_tumor <- sign(dmr_rep$GSE_T_minus_N) == sign(rowMeans(dmr_rep[, c("d_P3", "d_P4", "d_P5")])) &
  abs(dmr_rep$GSE_T_minus_N) > 0.05
write.csv(dmr_rep, file.path(TBL_DIR, "dmr_candidates_external_replication.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
dmr_rep
```

```{r pca-tumor, fig.cap="PCA built on Normal+Lesion only; tumor projected on top"}
nl_idx <- ss$Group %in% c("Normal", "Lesion")
top_nl <- order(matrixStats::rowVars(betas_f[, nl_idx]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:n_top]
pca_nl <- prcomp(t(betas_f[top_nl, nl_idx]), scale. = FALSE)
proj_t <- predict(pca_nl, t(betas_f[top_nl, !nl_idx, drop = FALSE]))

                    Sample = colnames(betas_f)[nl_idx])

p_df  <- dplyr::bind_rows(nl_df, t_df) |>
  left_join(ss, by = c("Sample" = "Sample_Name"))

pct_nl <- round(100 * pca_nl$sdev^2 / sum(pca_nl$sdev^2), 1)

ggplot(p_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = Group, shape = Patient)) +
```

# 8. Polycomb (PRC2) target enrichment + CIMP-style score

The top DMRs sit on HOX clusters and KRAB-ZNF arrays — the canonical
Polycomb-target / CGI hypermethylation signature seen in HNSCC and oral
cancer. This section tests whether the *whole* DMR list is enriched for
PRC2 targets, and computes a per-sample CIMP-PRC2 β score so the
Normal → Lesion → Tumor trajectory can be read off one figure.

```{r prc2-load, cache = TRUE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(missMethyl); library(msigdbr); library(org.Hs.eg.db)
})

m_cgp <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C2", subcollection = "CGP")
prc2_genes <- list(
  PRC2_targets       = unique(m_cgp$gene_symbol[m_cgp$gs_name == "BENPORATH_PRC2_TARGETS"]),
  SUZ12_targets      = unique(m_cgp$gene_symbol[m_cgp$gs_name == "BENPORATH_SUZ12_TARGETS"]),
  EED_targets        = unique(m_cgp$gene_symbol[m_cgp$gs_name == "BENPORATH_EED_TARGETS"]),
  ES_with_H3K27me3   = unique(m_cgp$gene_symbol[m_cgp$gs_name == "BENPORATH_ES_WITH_H3K27ME3"])
)
sapply(prc2_genes, length)
```

## 8a. Hypergeometric enrichment of DMR-overlapping genes for PRC2 targets

```{r prc2-enrich}
universe_genes <- unique(unlist(strsplit(na.omit(dmp$gene), ";")))
universe_genes <- universe_genes[nzchar(universe_genes)]

dmp_sig <- dmp[!is.na(dmp$P.Value) & dmp$P.Value < 1e-4 &
                 abs(dmp$delta_beta) > 0.1, ]
hit_genes <- unique(unlist(strsplit(na.omit(dmp_sig$gene), ";")))
hit_genes <- hit_genes[nzchar(hit_genes)]

prc2_test <- function(gene_set, hits, universe) {
  k <- sum(hits     %in% gene_set)
  K <- sum(universe %in% gene_set)
  n <- length(hits)
  N <- length(universe)
  data.frame(
    set         = NA_character_,
    set_size    = K,
    hits_in_set = k,
    hits_total  = n,
    universe    = N,
    expected    = round(n * K / N, 1),
    fold        = round((k / n) / (K / N), 2),
    p_hyper     = phyper(k - 1, K, N - K, n, lower.tail = FALSE)
  )
}
prc2_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(prc2_genes), function(nm) {
  out <- prc2_test(prc2_genes[[nm]], hit_genes, universe_genes)
  out$set <- nm; out
}))
prc2_table$adj_p <- p.adjust(prc2_table$p_hyper, method = "BH")
prc2_table
write.csv(prc2_table, file.path(TBL_DIR, "prc2_enrichment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r prc2-gsameth, cache = TRUE, cache.lazy = FALSE}
## More rigorous: array-bias-corrected CpG-level enrichment via missMethyl::gsameth.
## Requires uncollapsed EPIC v2 IlmnIDs.
sig_cpg_collapsed <- rownames(dmp_sig)
all_cpg_collapsed <- rownames(dmp)

## Map collapsed CpG IDs back to all v2 IlmnIDs that share that prefix.
expand_to_v2 <- function(cpg_collapsed, anno) {
  prefix <- sub("_[^_]+$", "", anno$Name)
  anno$Name[prefix %in% cpg_collapsed]
}
sig_v2 <- expand_to_v2(sig_cpg_collapsed, anno_v2)
all_v2 <- expand_to_v2(all_cpg_collapsed, anno_v2)

prc2_collections <- lapply(prc2_genes, function(symbols) {
  ids <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = symbols, column = "ENTREZID",
                keytype = "SYMBOL", multiVals = "first")
  ids[!is.na(ids)]
})

prc2_gsa <- gsameth(
  sig.cpg    = sig_v2,
  all.cpg    = all_v2,
  collection = prc2_collections,
  array.type = "EPIC_V2"
)
prc2_gsa$set <- rownames(prc2_gsa)
prc2_gsa <- prc2_gsa[, c("set","N","DE","P.DE","FDR")]
prc2_gsa
write.csv(prc2_gsa, file.path(TBL_DIR, "prc2_gsameth.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 8b. CIMP-PRC2 score per sample

For every CpG that (i) is in a CpG island and (ii) maps to a
BENPORATH_PRC2_TARGETS gene, compute the per-sample mean β. Plot the
Normal → Lesion → Tumor trajectory.

```{r cimp-prc2}
anno_v2_cpg <- anno_v2  # already deduped to one row per collapsed CpG
anno_v2_cpg$gene_first <- sub(";.*", "", anno_v2_cpg$UCSC_RefGene_Name)

prc2_panel <- anno_v2_cpg$cpg[
  anno_v2_cpg$Relation_to_Island == "Island" &
  anno_v2_cpg$gene_first %in% prc2_genes$PRC2_targets
]
prc2_panel <- intersect(prc2_panel, rownames(betas_f))
length(prc2_panel)

cimp_score <- colMeans(betas_f[prc2_panel, ], na.rm = TRUE)
cimp_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = names(cimp_score),
  CIMP_PRC2 = as.numeric(cimp_score)
) |> left_join(ss, by = c("Sample" = "Sample_Name"))
cimp_df

ggplot(cimp_df, aes(Group, CIMP_PRC2, group = Patient, colour = Group)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60", aes(group = Patient)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Patient), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = phen_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(y = "Mean β at PRC2-target CGI CpGs",
       x = NULL,
       title = sprintf("CIMP-PRC2 score (panel: %d CpGs)", length(prc2_panel))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

# 9. Field effect in the adjacent tissue

The first version of this section averaged β over the top-1000 paired DMPs.
That mixed hyper- and hypomethylated CpGs (which cancel), and it re-used DMPs
selected on the very adjacent samples being judged (circular). It is replaced
by the externally defined, composition-adjusted tumour signature from
GSE204943 (section 11), scored separately for hyper- and hypomethylated CpGs:
0 = GSE204943 normal mean, 1 = GSE204943 tumour mean.

```{r field-defect-external, eval = file.exists(file.path(EXT_DIR, "tables/tumor_likeness_pilot.csv"))}
fd_ext <- read.csv(file.path(EXT_DIR, "tables/tumor_likeness_pilot.csv"))
fd_ext[, c("Sample", "Group", "Epi", "hyper", "hypo", "tumor_likeness", "delta_vs_own_adj")]
write.csv(fd_ext, file.path(TBL_DIR, "field_defect_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Three of four adjacent samples score at or below the external normal range.
**P3-Adj (PVL patient) scores 0.63, as tumour-like as the lesions,** with
tumour-level hypermethylation, PMD erosion and a focal *CDKN2A* deletion
(section 12), and it scores higher than its own lesion. This is either field
involvement of the PVL "adjacent" mucosa or a lesion/adjacent label exchange.
The genotype check (section 12) rules out a swap between patients but cannot
tell P3's two samples apart; the histology of the exact tissue submitted for
the array should be reviewed.

# 10. DMR genomic-context breakdown + GO/KEGG enrichment

## 10a. Where do DMRs land?

```{r dmr-context, eval = exists("dmr_ranges") && length(dmr_ranges) > 0}
dmr_df_ctx <- as.data.frame(dmr_ranges) |>
  mutate(Direction = ifelse(meandiff > 0, "Hyper (Lesion>Normal)", "Hypo  (Lesion<Normal)"))

## map each DMR to its dominant CGI context by intersecting with anno_v2 CpGs
dmr_gr <- dmr_ranges
anno_gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(
  seqnames = anno_v2$chr,
  ranges   = IRanges::IRanges(anno_v2$pos, width = 1),
  cgi      = anno_v2$Relation_to_Island
)
ov <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(dmr_gr, anno_gr)
ctx_per_dmr <- tapply(anno_gr$cgi[S4Vectors::subjectHits(ov)],
                      S4Vectors::queryHits(ov),
                      function(x) names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1])
dmr_df_ctx$cgi_context <- NA_character_
dmr_df_ctx$cgi_context[as.integer(names(ctx_per_dmr))] <- unlist(ctx_per_dmr)

ctx_tab <- dmr_df_ctx |> count(Direction, cgi_context)
ggplot(ctx_tab, aes(cgi_context, n, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#e31a1c","#1f78b4")) +
  labs(x = "CpG-island relation", y = "DMR count", fill = NULL,
       title = "DMR distribution by CpG-island context") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

## 10b. GO + KEGG enrichment via missMethyl::gometh (EPIC v2)

```{r gometh, cache = TRUE, cache.lazy = FALSE}
sig_v2_strict <- expand_to_v2(rownames(dmp_sig), anno_v2)
all_v2_full   <- expand_to_v2(rownames(dmp),     anno_v2)

go_res <- gometh(sig.cpg = sig_v2_strict, all.cpg = all_v2_full,

kegg_top <- topGSA(kegg_res, number = 25)
```

# 11. External anchoring — GSE204943 (EPIC v1; 22 normal, 22 OPL, 74 OSCC)

Produced by `R/11_external_methylation.R`.

```{r ext-load, eval = file.exists(file.path(EXT_DIR, "external_methylation.rds"))}
ext <- readRDS(file.path(EXT_DIR, "external_methylation.rds"))
```

The pilot and GSE204943 share `r if (exists("ext")) format(ext$n_common, big.mark = ",")`
CpGs. Per-CpG mean β of the pilot adjacent tissue and GSE204943 normals
correlate at r = `r if (exists("ext")) round(ext$conc_r, 3)`, so the cohorts are
directly comparable despite the different pipelines (sesame noob vs minfi noob).

## 11a. A reproducible normal-to-tumour continuum (replaces manuscript Fig. 3B)

The tumour signature is learned in GSE204943 alone: limma on M-values, tumour
vs normal, **adjusted for epithelial and immune fraction and array plate**
(top 2,000 hyper- and 2,000 hypomethylated CpGs, FDR < 1e-6, |Δβ| > 0.2).
Each sample is scored per CpG as its position between the GSE204943 normal
mean (0) and tumour mean (1); the median is taken separately over hyper and
hypo CpGs and the two are averaged. GSE204943 OPL samples were not used to
pick CpGs, so their distribution is an out-of-sample reference.

```{r ext-continuum, out.width = "90%", eval = exists("ext")}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(EXT_DIR, "figures/continuum_external.png"))
ext$sc_p |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  select(Sample, histology, Epi, hyper, hypo, tumor_likeness, delta_vs_own_adj, purity_scaled)
```

In GSE204943 normals the score does not move with epithelial fraction
(lower panel), so composition alone does not generate it. Against their own
adjacent tissue, P4 (atypical hyperplasia), P5 (moderate–severe dysplasia,
later progressed) and the P2 tumour all shift strongly toward the tumour
state; P5's lesion scores the same as the tumour. The P3 pair runs the other
way (section 9). `purity_scaled` divides by the GSE204943 tumour trend at the
same epithelial fraction (secondary metric; extrapolates at very low Epi).

## 11b. Pilot projected into the GSE204943 methylation space

```{r ext-pca, out.width = "80%", eval = exists("ext")}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(EXT_DIR, "figures/pca_projection_gse204943.png"))
```

## 11c. Does each pilot lesion recapitulate the external tumour program?

Correlation, over the 4,000 signature CpGs, between the pilot
lesion-minus-own-adjacent Δβ and the GSE204943 tumour-minus-normal Δβ.

```{r ext-replication, eval = exists("ext")}
ext$rep_tab |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
ext$cons_sum |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

The second table takes CpGs that move > 0.1 in the same direction in all three
OPL pairs and asks how often they replicate (same direction, P < 0.05) in
GSE204943, against all other CpGs as background.

## 11d. PMD erosion and ZNF471 promoter methylation (the two GSE204943 programs)

PMD erosion = mean β of open-sea CpGs inside the GSE204943 tumour-hypomethylated
PMD blocks minus outside them (more negative = more eroded). Spearman with the
published GSE204943 per-sample PMD erosion score:
`r if (exists("ext")) round(ext$r_pmd, 2)` (sign reversed by construction).

```{r ext-pmd, out.width = "75%", eval = exists("ext")}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(EXT_DIR, "figures/pmd_znf471.png"))
ext$pz_p |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

## 11e. Promoter methylation of genes named in the manuscript

CGI/shore TSS-proximal CpGs, or all TSS200/TSS1500 CpGs for genes without a
CGI promoter. `d_Pn` = lesion/tumour minus own adjacent.

```{r ext-genes, eval = exists("ext")}
ext$gene_tab |> select(gene, n_cpg, cpg_type, GSE_Normal, GSE_OPL, GSE_Tumor, d_P2, d_P3, d_P4, d_P5) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

# 12. Copy number from the methylation array

Produced by `R/10_sigdf_qc_cnv.R`. Total probe intensity (noob, dye-bias
corrected, masked probes removed) is fitted against a reference
(conumee-style), binned at 50 probes and segmented with CBS (DNAcopy). Two
references: **LPO** = median of the *other* patients' adjacent tissue (detects
field events shared by a patient's adjacent and lesion); **paired** = the
patient's own adjacent (cancels germline CNVs and patient-specific signal
artefacts). HOX/ZIC clusters, whose intensity tracks methylation, are excluded,
and the GC-wave-prone terminal 5 Mb of each chromosome is not used for calls.

## 12a. Identity and sex

```{r cnv-identity, eval = file.exists(file.path(EXT_DIR, "cnv_objects.rds"))}
cnv <- readRDS(file.path(EXT_DIR, "cnv_objects.rds"))
round(cnv$conc, 2)       # genotype concordance, 65 rs probes
cnv$qc2
```

Each lesion matches its own adjacent tissue (0.95–1.00) and no other patient
(0.31–0.48): no sample swap between patients. All eight samples are female
(sesame inferSex; chrX β ~0.6, chrY intensity at background).

## 12b. Genome-wide profiles

```{r cnv-genome, out.width = "100%", eval = exists("cnv")}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(EXT_DIR, "figures/cnv_genome_LPO.png"))
```

```{r cnv-arms, eval = exists("cnv")}
cnv$arms |> filter(call != "") |>
  select(Sample, arm_label, LPO, paired, call, paired_confirmed, field_shared) |>
  mutate(across(c(LPO, paired), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

## 12c. 9p21.3 (*CDKN2A*/*MTAP*)

```{r cnv-9p21, out.width = "75%", eval = exists("cnv")}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(EXT_DIR, "figures/cnv_9p21_zoom.png"))
cnv$del9 |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

A deep focal deletion spanning *MTAP*–*CDKN2A*–*CDKN2B* (~21.6–22.2 Mb) is
present in P5-Lesion, P4-Lesion (not P4-Adj) and P3-Adj; in those samples the
region also has 1.6–2.4× the genome-wide pOOBAH failure rate, as expected for
a homozygous deletion in part of the cells. *CDKN2A* promoter methylation is
unchanged in these lesions (11e), so p16 is lost by deletion, not silencing.

# 13. External transcriptomic test — GSE227919

Produced by `R/12_external_rnaseq.R`. 66 leukoplakia biopsies (Control =
leukoplakia without dysplasia, HkNR, dysplasia, cancer); 25 non-cancer lesions
have follow-up (10 progressed to dysplasia or SCC). Program scores are the
mean per-gene z-score of log2(normalised count + 1). Trend = Spearman with
histologic class; progression = AUC (bootstrap 95% CI) and a logistic model
adjusted for histologic class.

```{r rna-tests, eval = file.exists(file.path(EXT_DIR, "external_rnaseq.rds"))}
rna <- readRDS(file.path(EXT_DIR, "external_rnaseq.rds"))
rna$res |> select(set, n_genes, trend_rho, trend_fdr, prog_AUC, prog_AUC_lo, prog_AUC_hi,
                  prog_wilcox_p, prog_fdr, prog_p_adj_class) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 2)))
```

Histologic class alone gives AUC = `r if (exists("rna")) round(rna$hist_auc, 2)` for progression.

```{r rna-figs, out.width = "90%", eval = exists("rna")}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(EXT_DIR, "figures/rnaseq_programs_by_class.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(EXT_DIR, "figures/rnaseq_programs_progression.png"))
```

# 14. Methods audit (October 2026)

| Item | Problem in v1 | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Sex inference | `inferSex()` given a SigDF; errored, NA for all samples | Pass betas; all 8 female |
| Detection rate | Counted design/quality masks as failures | pOOBAH rate reported separately |
| PCA / manuscript Fig. 3A | PC1 read as malignancy; r = 0.90 with epithelial fraction | EpiDISH added; composition-adjusted external continuum (11a) |
| Manuscript Fig. 3B | Hand-drawn curve, not derivable from the PCA, no method | Replaced by 11a (fully specified, external anchor) |
| DMRs | 8,090 "DMRs" built at cpg.annotate FDR 0.5; no CpG passes FDR | Labelled exploratory; top candidates checked in GSE204943 (6b) |
| PRC2 / GO enrichment | Hit list from nominal P < 1e-4 | Labelled exploratory; per-sample CIMP-PRC2 score unaffected |
| Field-defect score | Mean β mixed hyper and hypo CpGs; DMPs selected on the same samples | External signed signature (section 9) |
| Copy number | Not assessed on the array | Added (section 12); checks WES/XHMM calls |

# 15. Save processed object

```{r save}
processed <- list(
  betas        = betas_f,
  mvals        = mvals,
  sample_sheet = ss,
  dmp_table    = dmp,
  dmr_ranges   = if (exists("dmr_ranges")) dmr_ranges else NULL,
  pca          = pca,
  pca_nl       = pca_nl,
  qc           = qc,
  session      = sessionInfo()
)
saveRDS(processed, file.path(OUT_DIR, "processed.rds"))
```

# 16. Caveats

* **n = 1 tumor.** Any tumor-involving comparison is descriptive only;
  p-values are reported only for the paired Normal vs Lesion contrast.
* **Single chip / single row position per sample.** Row-position effects
  cannot be modeled because every sample is on a different row.
* **Bulk tissue.** Epithelial fraction ranges from 0.10 to 0.86 across the
  eight samples and drives the unsupervised structure (section 4b). Use the
  composition-adjusted external score (section 11) for any malignancy claim.
* **External cohort.** GSE204943 is a gingivobuccal, largely tobacco-chewing
  Indian cohort on EPIC v1; the pilot is EPIC v2. Paired (lesion minus own
  adjacent) quantities are the most robust to the platform/population offset.
* **P3 labels.** P3-Adj looks more neoplastic than P3-Lesion on methylation and
  copy number; confirm against the histology of the submitted tissue.

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
